name: LLM-FP4 (4-bit floating-point W4A4 PTQ, pre-Blackwell)
bits: w4a4 (both weights and activations quantized to 4-bit FLOATING POINT, post-training)
activation_scheme: FP4 rather than INT4: exponent-bit count and clipping range are searched for optimality per layer, which the paper argues is what determines FP-quantization performance. Activation handling is the notable part - the paper identifies high INTER-channel variance and low INTRA-channel variance in activation distributions as consistent across LLMs, BERT and ViTs, and applies PER-CHANNEL activation quantization, then REPARAMETERIZES the extra per-channel scales as exponential biases of the weights at negligible cost.
kernels: nbasyl/LLM-FP4 research code. No hardware FP4 path existed when this was written (Oct 2023) - FP4 tensor cores arrived with Blackwell in 2024.
quality_delta: From the abstract: quantizes both weights and activations of LLaMA-13B to 4-bit, achieving an average score of 63.1 on commonsense zero-shot reasoning tasks, 'only 5.8 lower than the full-precision model' and 'significantly outperforming the previous state-of-the-art by 12.7 points'. Authors' own numbers; no independent replication located.
notes: IMPORTANT NAME COLLISION WARNING: this is 'LLM-FP4' (arXiv 2310.16836), NOT NVFP4. The repo already has an nvfp4 record for NVIDIA's Blackwell block-scaled E2M1 format. They share a bit width and a float element format but nothing else - different era, different authors, different format, and only one of them has hardware behind it. Do not let anyone merge these two records. Included here because it is the clearest pre-Blackwell demonstration that genuine W4A4 (4-bit weights AND 4-bit activations) was achievable before any 4-bit tensor core existed, which is exactly the regime that the w4a16-vs-w4a4 distinction turns on: LLM-FP4's arithmetic was emulated, so it was a compression win, not a compute win, and would not necessarily run faster than fp16 on the hardware available to it. The per-channel activation scales folded into the weights as exponential biases is the same reparameterization trick as OmniQuant's LET and SmoothQuant's migration - three independent papers converging on 'make the weights absorb the activation difficulty'. SCHEME RECLASSIFIED (parent agent, 2026-10-03): scheme was 'wq4a4' (a proxy recorded while the enum lacked a legal value) and is now 'llm-fp4'.
